Most small businesses have something in common: they are run by reluctant operators. These are owners who set out to provide a service to their local community, and ended up running a business instead. They did not sign up to become finance people, HR people, recruiters, billers, or claims specialists. They became those things because someone had to.

Dental practices are a perfect example. Dentists go to school to practice dentistry and care for patients. Instead many are stuck doing paperwork, hiring people, training and retaining staff, negotiating insurance contracts, fighting claims, and managing cash flow.

Across roughly 160,000 dental practices in the U.S., this work is increasingly hard to staff and expensive to get wrong. AI can already do much of this work today. It is just not in the hands of these businesses yet.

We think businesses will soon run themselves, and small businesses will be among the first. Today, we are thrilled to announce that a16z is leading Lassie’s $35 million Series A – and partnering with a team solving exactly this problem.

Lassie is building AI that runs small businesses, starting with dental practices. Co-founders Steijn Pelle and Frédéric Renken did not find this problem from a distance. After working in consumer fintech at Robinhood and Coinbase, Steijn learned from his own dentist, Dr. Kwon, how complex the financial administration of an SMB dental practice can be. He and Frédéric, who had built product at Superhuman and Uber, then worked inside Dr. Kwon’s office, processing payments by hand to understand the workflow from the inside.

This story is emblematic of how Steijn and Frédéric have approached building Lassie. Before writing a single line of code, they spent months talking to dentists, primary care doctors, and healthcare finance teams. Then they spent years building the infrastructure and integrations required for agents to operate directly within a practice’s workflow: reading insurance claims, reconciling payments, posting to the ledger, and flagging claims that need action. Lassie is not a copilot that creates more work for the practice to review. It does the work.

Lassie already works with more than 700 practices across 49 states, generates more than $10 million in annualized revenue, and provides practices with 250,000 hours of labor a year. Growth has come largely through referrals and inbound demand – a sign that customers are not just buying the product, but telling other practice owners about it. The most important benefit, customers say, is not simply doing the work faster. It is catching the underpayments, denials, and missing claims that used to slip through.

Dental is a strong first market because the pain is acute and the workflows are structured, repetitive, and high-value. But the larger insight is not dental-specific. Every small business is still held together by human labor: people answer phones, schedule work, hire and train staff, chase paperwork, collect payments, reconcile accounts, follow up on exceptions, and keep the business moving. The last generation of software gave businesses better tools. AI agents change the unit of value from software to labor. Lassie is starting with dental, but the broader opportunity is much larger: the small business that runs itself.

That is also why Lassie is difficult to replicate with a generic model alone. Running a small business is not one task; it is thousands of recurring workflows across customers, vendors, payments, forms, systems, and exceptions. The product has to understand the business, connect to the tools where work happens, know when to act, and know when to ask. Over time, the product learns from every completed workflow, building a knowledge layer that is difficult to recreate from scratch.

We are thrilled to partner with Steijn, Frédéric, and the Lassie team as they build toward one of the most important shifts in software: from tools that help businesses operate to agents that do the work. # How Steijn Pelle built Lassie to help small businesses run themselves using AI

### 800+ small businesses across the country are using Lassie to run themselves, and Steijn just raised another $35M to take Lassie to the next level

Katie Kirsch and Cola Gahm

Aug 24, 2026

13

1

2

Share

AI is getting rapidly adopted by Fortune 500 companies and law firms… but what about the millions of small businesses that keep the world running, like your local doctor, plumber, or auto-mechanic?

It turns out, small businesses are more eager to adopt AI than you might think. In fact, hundreds of businesses across the US are now already partly running themselves using AI - including managing paperwork, updating their systems, and soon, interacting and transacting with customers - thanks to Lassie.

Lassie is building the autonomous systems that take care of all the busywork behind running a small business - so that owners can finally focus on what they do best (their craft) and get their time back.

Since founding the company a few years ago, Steijn Pelle has scaled Lassie to 800+ small businesses across 49 states, starting with doctors’ offices. A few months ago, he raised a $35M Series A led by a16z, bringing the company’s total funding to $47M. Now, he’s on a mission to scale Lassie - and create a future world where every small business runs itself, using AI.

---

steijnpelle@steijnpelleToday, we're introducing Lassie and $47M in funding led by a16z. We're building AI that runs small businesses, starting with doctors' offices. Lassie is already trusted by 700+ practices across the country, working autonomously to provide them with 30 hours of labor per month. 2:49 PM · Jun 3, 2026 · 1.19M Views203 Replies · 151 Reposts · 2.91K Likes

---

### The founding story

Before founding Lassie, Steijn was one of the first product managers at both Robinhood and Coinbase - and always had a passion for solving hard problems with technology.

The idea for Lassie came out of a conversation he had with his own doctor, Dr. Kwon, in Menlo Park, CA. Dr. Kwon shared with Steijn that the most challenging part of running his own business wasn’t the craft - it was the 200+ hours per month that he and his team spent on paperwork.

All the tedious, manual, detail-oriented work that they struggled to find staff members to do, and that Dr. Kwon was forced to do himself after-hours - like managing insurance payments, catching underpaid claims, appealing denials, and going back and forth with patients on bills and appointments.

Steijn could sense that there was a huge business opportunity here. Millions of small businesses each spend tens (if not hundreds) of thousands of dollars per year on the kind of busywork that Dr. Kwon was describing.

From left to right: Frédéric Renken, Dr. Kwon, and Steijn Pelle

Steijn also knew it could take years of unglamorous work to fully understand the busywork required to run small businesses - let alone, build a solution that would autonomously run it for business owners in a way that complied with a complex, manual, and highly-regulated industry.

Most founders would have looked right past this space (what Paul Graham calls, “ schlep blindness”) or given up. But for that rare founder with the patience and grit to figure things out from first principles - the reward would be enormous.

This was an opportunity to capture an underserved market that was desperate for a solution to automate the thousands of uninteresting, overlooked tasks that bottleneck small businesses every single day, on a recurring basis.

“AI that autonomously runs small businesses” is what Lassie’s new board member Alex Rampell would call a“Goldilocks zone” - a market that’s not the main priority for frontier AI labs to own themselves, and too messy for a generic model to serve, but big enough to matter.

Maybe it was the competitive runner in him - or that he had seen enough close friends train for years and compete in the Olympics - but Steijn wasn’t afraid of playing the long game. In fact, it was exactly the challenge he had been looking for.

---

### Bringing Lassie to life

You have to learn how to walk before you can run. For Steijn and his team, that meant - you have to learn how to run a small business yourself, before you can train AI to do it for you. So, Steijn and his team signed up to take on all the paperwork for two different doctors’ offices - Dr. Kwon’s in Menlo Park, and a gastroenterologist’s in Scranton. And they didn’t just do this for a few days, then quit - they did this manual work for a year.

To give an example day in the life, Steijn would comb through hundreds of payments from an insurance portal, enter them into the practice management system one by one, print a forty-page list of patients who needed a bill, and finish the day checking everyone’s balances and generating statements. Steijn smiles while thinking about those days: “I felt like Jim Halpert from The Office!”

Co-founders Frédéric Renken (left) and Steijn Pelle (right)

After he and his team figured out the jobs to be done, they started training autonomous systems to do the work for them. Given that they were operating in such a hands-on, heavily-regulated space, handling sensitive financial and personal health information (PHI) - there was no room for error. Lassie didn’t just have to be good, it had to be correct. It took several more years for the product to be ready to scale.

One of the things that had impressed Steijn most at Robinhood was how relentlessly the team worked to seamlessly onboard new users - with little to no manual account approval. Similarly at Superhuman, where his co-founder Frédéric Renken was the first product hire, the team had obsessed over removing friction at the critical moment when people first touch the product.

To learn how to sell and deploy AI at scale, Steijn and his team started by taking the non-scalable approach: first, doing it all in-person. They spent more than a year traveling around the country to visit small business owners, sit with them at their computers, and personally install Lassie onto their systems. Through this, Steijn and his team built a winning playbook for codifying the sale and productizing the implementation of Lassie at scale. Along the way, they also converted their first 100 earliest adopters into some of the biggest champions for the company.

Dr. Kwon is one of those proud early adopters of Lassie - now able to see almost twice as many patients and still make it home in time for dinner with his family. Many customers like him are clinking champagne to celebrate the time Lassie is saving them. Someone recently told Steijn that Lassie “saved his marriage.”

---

### Building the culture and team that scales

A lot has changed since Steijn’s earliest days of building Lassie, but some things haven’t. His approach to operating at the lowest level of detail first, doing things with rigor of thought, and valuing the craft of building something wonderful- is clearly deeply rooted into the company’s culture.

The team is all in. 15 people, in-person in San Francisco, sprinting to make Lassie the AI company that makes entrepreneurship easier for all small businesses. In their first 90 days at the company, every new team member spends time working in a few real small businesses, just like Steijn and Frédéric once did - so they know what it’s like to schlep (err, step) in small business owners’ shoes.

When asked about the most important team values at Lassie, Steijn is quick to answer - the Lassie team doesn’t ship junk, likes rigor of thought, and cares about direct communication.

Steijn is planning to triple the Lassie team in the next year - and he’s about to open a brand-new office in Jackson Square, complete with an open kitchen, beautiful Scandinavian-style co-working spaces, and an in-house chef who previously worked for the Collison brothers.

A glimpse into Lassie’s new San Francisco office

Ultimately, Steijn is in this for the long haul - a marathon of sprints, if you will - and he’s looking for people who are just as persistent and passionate about solving hard problems. If that sounds like you, come build Lassie with him.

---

### Open Roles

Lassie is hiring across the board. A few open roles that stand out:

Deployment Strategist- Be on the frontlines of getting AI deployed to small businesses. And with that build the playbooks for implementation, account management, and maintain the bar for turning customers into fans. Together with the people that did this for Superhuman and Robinhood.

Head of Marketing- Build Lassie’s growth marketing engine that helps to make millions of small business owners aware that AI can now help them run their business.

Product Engineer- Build the products small businesses use every day to get work done without adding more work to manage.

Head of Finance- As Lassie’s first finance hire, you’ll build the AI-native financial operations from scratch alongside CEO Steijn Pelle and advisor Jason Warnick (former CFO, Robinhood) - owning everything from monthly close, strategic finance projects like pricing, and building the operating model, to supporting future fundraises.

Founding Recruiter- Help recruit a world-class team that can bring AI to millions of small businesses across the world.

Most doctors that we met, they really just wanted to kind of serve their community and and be a great doctor. Wow. And that's just really freed us ought to focus on the patient experience. Seeing what Lassie can do is incredible and it's something that I can't imagine any practice won't benefit tremendously. # I’m joining Coinbase

3 min read

Apr 9, 2018

2

Press enter or click to view image in full size

It’s been a busy few months, and it’s time to share exciting news: I’ve joined Coinbase as a product lead to scale the company’s growth team! This is an amazing opportunity to share my learnings about user growth and apply it to cryptocurrency.

It also feels very special to me coming from Amsterdam, where the first Stock Exchange was established in 1602, to work with the team in San Francisco to bring an open financial system to millions of people worldwide.

## Why Coinbase, and why now?

Three big reasons:

### 1. Digital currency increases economic freedom

I agree with

(Coinbase CEO and Co-Founder) that digital currency may be the most effective way to foster and increase economic freedom: the potential positive impact of digital currencies is staggering. They may accelerate the economic development of countries, increase the quality of life for billions of people, and facilitate capital deployment needed to drive innovation around the globe.

It’s still a young company, but I firmly believe that Coinbase can and will play a leading role in the transition to a global open financial system.

### 2. The Coinbase values

Values are important to me. I joined Coinbase because I’ve been impressed by a highly motivated, intelligent, and ambitious group of people aligned around four core values essential to achieving this mission: efficient execution, continuous learning, clear communication, and positive energy.

I’m looking forward to carry the growth mindset — of deeply understanding customers, striving for big impact, efficient execution, and a strong sense of purpose — with me to Coinbase.

### 3. The opportunity to learn user growth at scale

The world is standing at the precipice of an economic revolution. Digital currencies change the game in many ways, and making these changes in the right ways is essential.

The opportunity to scale the user base of a principled and successful company — that is already positively shaping the future of this new form of exchange — is thrilling.

This is a rare opportunity in a rare moment. As Marc Andreessen, Co-Founder of Netscape and Andreessen Horowitz(a Coinbase investor) explains so well, digital currency (like Bitcoin, Ethereum or Litecoin) is one of the greatest examples of the power of network effects since the advent of the Internet.

## Let’s get started

I would not have arrived at this point without the friendship and guidance of many good friends, advisors, and others who simply made time for sharing, teaching and learning. Thank you to each of you for your help.

Looking ahead, I see a mountain for us to climb. The path is steep, and there are ambitious years ahead on the way to reaching the top. I’m delighted to embark on this journey with such an amazing group of people. For me it’s Day One at base camp — and I can’t wait to get started.

If you’re an engineer, data scientist or designer: contact me if you’re interested in joining me on this journey of building a growth team for Coinbase.

Join Pete in conversation with Steijn Pelle, Co-Founder and CEO of Lassie, the AI healthcare admin worker transforming how doctors run their practices.

Steijn and Pete dig into Lassie's fascinating journey from Steijn literally working in his dentist's back office to building a company on track for $100M ARR within a year. They cover Lassie's crazy commitment to product quality (they actually flew to 100+ dental offices nationwide to install their software!), their ruthless "say NO to most leads" ICP discipline, and why they waited until hundreds of customers before making their first sales hire.

You'll love Steijn's stories about turning one delighted dentist into an organic growth engine, why they run 40-50 hour work trials for sales candidates, and their "Robinhood-style" waitlist approach that keeps them laser-focused on delighting every customer they take.

Steijn's consumer growth background at Coinbase and Robinhood shaped Lassie's unique approach to B2B sales – focusing on turning customers into superfans rather than just closing deals. Their "wedge product" strategy targeting the 80-100 monthly hours doctors spend processing insurance payments has positioned them to capture the entire $100-200K in admin OPEX practices currently waste.

https://www.golassie.com/

Sales motion details: AI admin automation for healthcare practices, independent doctor-owners target persona, five-figure ACVs, short sales cycles with extremely qualified leads, primarily word-of-mouth acquisition.

## Executive Summary

When Steijn Pelle visited his dentist Dr. Kwon's office in Menlo Park, his jaw dropped—not from dental work, but from seeing stacks of paper payments being manually processed in the back office. This Silicon Valley dentist, rated #1 in Palo Alto, was spending 80-100 hours monthly reconciling insurance payments by hand. Recognizing a massive opportunity, Pelle and co-founder Frederik embedded themselves in Dr. Kwon's practice, manually taking over his accounts receivable process before building software to replace themselves. Their company, Lassie, has grown exponentially by creating an "AI healthcare admin worker" that automates the financial operations of independent medical practices. With five-figure ACVs and a clear path to capturing the $100-200K in admin annual OPEX that practices currently spend, Lassie is on track to hit $100M ARR within 12 months. Their success stems from an obsessive focus on product quality and extreme ICP discipline that turns customers into vocal advocates who drive organic growth through powerful word-of-mouth referrals.

## Key Metrics

Target Market: 1 million independent healthcare practices across the US, starting with dentists

Primary Persona: Currently, Dentist-owners of independent dental practices (later, doctor owners of healthcare practices)

Current Growth: Exponential, projecting $100M ARR within 12 months

Average Contract Value: Five-figure annual contracts

Sales Cycle: Short cycles with high conversion from extremely targeted prospects

Initial Sales Team: Founder-led until hundreds of customers before first sales hire

Customer Acquisition: Primarily word-of-mouth referrals from delighted customers

## Problem Discovery: Finding $200,000 of Wasted Time in Every Doctor's Office

When Steijn Pelle moved to Silicon Valley from the Netherlands, he brought a unique combination of sales talent and product obsession honed through 15 years of startup experience. After working at Coinbase and Robinhood during their early growth phases, he was looking for his next challenge when his dentist, Dr. Kwon, made an unexpected request: "Steijn, you work in fintech—do you want to know how I run my finances?"

What Pelle saw behind the scenes shocked him. "My jaw dropped because he's a very forward-thinking doctor...and yet he's sitting in front of stacks of paper with his team, processing payments by hand," Stein recalls. He discovered that independent health practices—the second largest SMB vertical in America after retail/restaurants—were completely underserved by technology.

The average doctor's office spends an astonishing 200 hours monthly on paperwork: manually submitting insurance claims, reconciling payments, and billing patients. "In a time we are ready to send people to Mars, our docs and their teams spend the entire day Jim Carrey-ing their way through life," Pelle explains. Dr. Kwon, despite tripling his practice's revenue, was personally spending tens of hours monthly sitting in front of accounts receivable paperwork.

The initial assumption Pelle got wrong? That this was a technology problem. Through methodical research—spending nine months talking to practices across multiple specialties and embedding himself in their operations—he realized the real issue was a compliance and workflow problem that technology alone couldn't fix. Success would require a much deeper understanding of healthcare's specific financial workflows.

## Early Sales Development: From Manual Labor to Five-Figure Contracts

Pelle and co-founder Frederik took an unorthodox approach to winning their first customer. Instead of building a product and hoping someone would buy it, they did the exact opposite: they convinced Dr. Kwon to let them manually take over his accounts receivable process first.

"We first listened to all his problems," Pelle explains. "Then we went back to him and said: 'I think we can fix your problems, but we need to come work for you 9-to-5 to actually do the job.'" This hands-on approach gave them intimate knowledge of the pain points while immediately delivering value.

The mental model that transformed their approach was maintaining laser focus on a specific wedge product, inspired by Robinhood's early days. "What I really loved about Robinhood is they started with a very small wedge," Pelle says. "iPhone app only, the rest was on the waitlist. Android and web weren't available. You could only trade 5,000 shares—no options, no crypto, no retirement accounts."

Lassie took the same approach, zeroing in on just one high-value problem: automating insurance payment reconciliation. "Out of the 200 hours practices spend monthly on paperwork, 80-100 hours go to processing insurance payments," Pelle notes. "They literally open envelopes and update their ERP by hand, patient by patient, cash the checks, and make sure all the numbers add up."

This narrow focus allowed them to build an exceptional solution for a single pain point rather than spreading themselves thin across multiple features. The result? Their wedge product alone commands a five-figure annual contract value, with a clear expansion path to capture the entire $100-200K in administrative OPEX that practices currently spend.

## Skills Building: Converting Consumer Growth DNA into B2B Success

Pelle didn't come from a traditional B2B sales background. His experience was in consumer growth at Coinbase and Robinhood, where he worked on referral programs and user onboarding. This unconventional background proved advantageous—he approached healthcare practice sales with a product-led mentality that prioritized activation and delight.

"I got lucky," Pelle admits when asked about overcoming sales fears. "According to my parents, as an 8-year-old boy, I sold carrots from my parents' garden. In high school, I was a wedding DJ, which really helped me understand how humans are wired. In college, I started a fashion company where we sold suits and ties online and through department stores."

This natural inclination toward selling combined with his growth expertise created a unique approach. Rather than focusing on closing deals, Pelle obsessed over turning customers into advocates who would drive organic growth—exactly as he'd seen happen at Robinhood, where according to their S-1 filing, "70% of all new funded accounts came through organic growth and referral."

To sharpen his B2B skills, Pelle relied on several key resources:

"Founding Sales" by Pete Kazanjy (which he kept referencing throughout his journey)

"Crossing the Chasm" for understanding how to sell to early adopters

"Four Steps to Epiphany" and "How to Talk to Humans" for customer development

YC content, especially Paul Graham's articles

Lenny's newsletter for benchmarking metrics

The most important lesson came from his consumer growth background: "A lot of founders came to me asking how to scale their growth efforts. In 99% of cases, my honest advice was: work on product-market fit first." This perspective shaped Lassie's entire approach to sales—get the product right, focus on turning customers into fans, and organic growth will follow.

## Sales Process Evolution: From Hand-Drawn Fish to Scaled Success

Lassie's sales motion began with pure founder-led selling and evolved methodically as they scaled. "We were founder-led up until $1M ARR, doing a freaking good job for Dr. Kwon, which got us referrals from his wife, people he studied with, and his friends," Pelle explains.

The organic growth they generated served as crucial validation that they were building something valuable. Customers were referring colleagues without incentives—a powerful signal that Lassie was solving a genuine pain point in a remarkable way.

# Fitmo Raises €1.2M in Funding

 By FinSMEs 

-

November 24, 2014

Fitmo, an Amsterdam, The Netherlands-based fitness app startup, raised €1.2m in funding.

Informal backers made the investment.

Led by Co-founder/CEO Dave Roeloffs and Co-founder/COO Steijn Pelle, Fitmo has developed the Fitmo coach that connects and motivates clients via the app and provides clients with personalized workout schedules that clients can complete on their own time.

The company has also announced integration data with UP by Jawbone, the wristband, app and data system that allows users to understand how they move, eat and sleep. Fitmo adds the human factor to technology by making personal training services available to all. With the integration, Fitmo will be listed in the UP App Gallery (amongst apps such as Runkeeper and Strava) providing members of the UP community with the option to link to the Fitmo app to receive coaching with a professional coach.

[Peter Driessen](https://www.linkedin.com/pub/peter-driessen/85/149/432), founder of games producer Spil Games, invests in Amsterdam based fitness app startup Fitmo.
Driessen bought an undisclosed share in the startup to help Fitmo grow in the next 12 months and attract international investors.
“Peter is an experienced entrepreneur that has the expertise we need to take the next steps”, says Fitmo co-founder Steijn Pelle.
Driessen got involved with Fitmo for its “interesting concept in a growing health market”, he says.
#### Personal trainer
The people behind[Fitmo](http://www.fitmo.com/)developed an app that takes the personal trainer online and mobile. It allows users to train with an experienced coach that sets up a tailored program and advice, for example via video calls.
The startup raised €1.2M in funding from informal investors last year and[signed a deal](https://startupjuncture.com/2014/11/21/fitness-app-fitmo-raises-e1-2m-signs-deal-jawbone/)with consumer technology company Jawbone, known for its Fitness Up wristband.

Het gaat lekker met Fitmo. De Amsterdamse startup die échte personal trainers op een betaalbare manier koppelt met mensen die aan hun gezondheidsdoelen willen werken heeft de oprichter van Spil Games Peter Driessen als investeerder aangetrokken. “Fitmo heeft een sterk team en is een zeer interessant concept in een grote, groeiende gezondheids markt”, aldus Driessen.

## Een personal trainer in je broekzak

Door de personal trainers op afstand te laten werken en de tools te bieden die zij nodig hebben om online 1 op 1 te trainen, is een coach via Fitmo (vanaf EUR 8 per maand) een stuk beter betaalbaar dan een coach die je in real life begeleid (vanaf EUR 25 per uur), en kunnen coaches tot wel 100 klanten tegelijk managen. Fitmo haalde afgelopen najaar een investering van 1,2 miljoen euro op en sloot een samenwerking met Jawbone. Door de samenwerking met Jawbone, dat bekend is geworden door de fitness-armband Jawbone Up, kan Fitmo de data uit de wearables van Jawbone gebruiken om naar de personal trainer te sturen.

“Met Peter halen we een ervaren ondernemer aan boord. Iemand die met zijn achtergrond ons team vele lessen kan leren over het begeleiden van onstuimige groei van een internet bedrijf, het bouwen van een team en het aantrekken van internationale investeerders”, zegt Steijn Pelle (co-founder van Fitmo).

## Uitbreiding

Gelijktijdig zijn ook Martijn de Kuijper(oprichter Yuno, oprichter Fosbury) en Bram Kanstein(oprichter Startup Stash, ex Product Hunt) bij het team betrokken om het concept naar een volgend niveau te brengen. Afgelopen maanden heeft Fitmo gewerkt aan het bereiken van een product/market fit. De focus voor het komende jaar ligt op groei en het traject richting een Serie A investeringsronde. Het bedrag dat Peter Driessen in de startup steekt, wordt niet bekend gemaakt.

## Fitmo

Fitmo is in 2014 opgericht door Dave Roeloffs en Steijn Pelle. Zij vinden dat het voor iedereen in deze wereld mogelijk moet zijn om op een betaalbare manier gezondheidsdoelen te halen. Dit doen zij door middel van een marktplaats waar ze échte personal coaches online in contact brengen met nieuwe klanten.

# Booming: App die sporters en trainers bij elkaar brengt

RTL Z·14 november 2014·Aangepast: 6 september 2015

Fitnessplatform en startup Fitmo heeft in een mum van tijd 1,2 miljoen euro opgehaald bij investeerders. Wie de investeerders zijn wil Fitmo niet zeggen, maar het gaat om particulieren. Maak RTL je Google-favoriet

De investeerders zijn er vroeg bij want Fitmo gaat deze week pas open voor het grote publiek. Sinds augustus is het sportplatform al te gebruiken door genodigden.

Fitmo verdient geld door mensen die willen sporten te koppelen aan een personal trainer. Klanten betalen ongeveer 40 euro per maand. Fitmo krijgt daar 20 procent van en de rest gaat naar de trainer.

VerdienmodelHet verdienmodel is te vergelijken met dat van Airbnb en Uber: Fitmo brengt vraag en aanbod bij elkaar. Volgens Dave Roelofs, één van de twee oprichters, is het Fitmo vooral handig voor mensen die wel willen sporten, maar een extra duwtje in de rug nodig hebben. ‘Er zijn al veel gezondheids-apps, maar die zijn te generiek, omdat wij werken met mensen denken we echt iets toe te voegen.’

Inmiddels hebben 400 klanten zich ingeschreven bij Fitmo, zij maken – via de app - gebruik van veertig personal trainers. Klanten kunnen videobellen of chatten met de personal trainer. Tijdens het eerste gesprek bespreken ze de doelen. Vervolgens stelt de trainer een schema op.

Jawbone, één van de grootste makers van fitnessbandjes, heeft zich inmiddels gemeld bij Fitmo. De twee gaan een samenwerking aan waarbij Jawbone op termijn gebruikers actief gaat wijzen op de diensten van Fitmo. Ook zou de personal trainer automatisch een waarschuwing kunnen krijgen als uit de data die de fitnesstracker verzameld, blijkt dat zijn pupil zich niet aan het trainingsschema houdt.

BuitenlandNederland veroveren is voor de startup niet genoeg. The real split comes down to automation depth, integration flexibility (think voice AI receptionists, insurance verification tools, and AI charting add-ons), and the manual work that stays with your team after go-live. Below, we compare five leading dental PMS options across integration ecosystem, automation depth, cloud vs. on-premise architecture, data ownership, multi-location support, and implementation lift. We also cover Lassie, an AI automation layer that works alongside your PMS to handle insurance payment posting and reconciliation, the back-office work that every PMS leaves on staff. Dentrix and Eaglesoft for mature all-in-one setups, Open Dental for customization, Curve and Denticon for cloud-native architecture, and Lassie for the insurance automation none of them include.

TLDR:

- Five dental PMS options compared by integration depth, automation, cloud architecture, and multi-location support, plus Lassie as an insurance back-office automation add-on
- Dentrix and Eaglesoft run in 35,000+ and 30,000 practices, but require on-premise IT overhead
- Open Dental starts at $199/month with full data ownership and anytime export rights
- Cloud options like Curve and Denticon remove server management but vary by practice size and fit
- Lassie automates EOB posting and bank reconciliation for practices on Dentrix, Eaglesoft, or Open Dental

## What is Dental Practice Management Software?

Dental practice management software (PMS) is the system of record a dental office runs on. It holds patient charts, schedules, treatment plans, imaging, insurance claims, and ledgers in one place, so the front desk, hygienists, and dentists work from the same data. According to Grand View Research, the dental PMS market is projected to grow from $3.3 billion in 2026 to $6.8 billion by 2033, driven by the adoption of automation.

Clinically, a PMS stores radiographs, periodontal charts, and treatment notes. Administratively, it handles scheduling, eligibility checks, claim submission, payment posting, and patient billing. If a workflow touches a patient or a payer, it usually lives inside the PMS.

## How We Ranked Dental Practice Management Software

We weighed five PMS platforms (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, Curve, and Denticon) against the criteria that move the needle for dental practices in 2026. Lassie is covered separately as an insurance automation add-on that works alongside any of these systems, not as a PMS itself:

- Integration ecosystem. The most important factor. A PMS that opens cleanly to voice AI receptionists, insurance verification, AI charting, and recall tools lets you build the stack you want. Automated insurance verification eliminates hours of work and reduces claim denials substantially.
- Automation depth. How much of EOB posting, claims, and reconciliation runs without a human touching it.
- Architecture. Cloud vs. on-premises servers: what that means for uptime, updates, and IT overhead.
- Data ownership. Whether you can pull your records out in a usable format if you leave.
- Multi-location support. Shared tax IDs, separate ledgers, centralized reporting.
- Implementation lift. Onboarding time, training burden, and schedule disruption.

## Best Insurance Back-Office Automation for Dental Practices: Lassie

Lassie tackles the part of running a dental practice that every PMS leaves on staff: insurance payment posting and reconciliation. We read EOBs, post them into your PMS, and match against bank deposits with no manual keying.

### What Lassie does well

- Real-time EOB posting with custom rules for adjustments, write-offs, and downgrades
- Bank reconciliation to the cent, flagging overpayments and discrepancies
- Multi-location support across shared or separate tax IDs with location-level ledger routing
- Free EFT enrollment to kill paper checks and virtual credit card fees
- Automated secondary claim filing for Open Dental practices on Dental Exchange
- Cancel-anytime contracts, unlimited training, and direct account manager access
- Automated patient billing with statement generation, SMS delivery, and real-time flagging of unpaid balances after 30 days

### Where Lassie fits

Lassie works alongside your existing PMS, it does not replace it. You keep Dentrix, Eaglesoft, or Open Dental for scheduling, charting, and clinical workflows; Lassie handles the insurance payment posting and reconciliation those systems leave to staff. Practices that file at least 70 percent of payments through commercial PPOs get the most value. Denticon users and practices with heavy Medicaid volume through Skygen-style administrators are not a fit yet.

### Trade-offs to know

Claim submission and aging follow-up stay with the staff. Automated appeals generation is now available in beta. Setup is $3,000 per location, and groups under a shared TIN must onboard every location at once.

Based on Lassie's customer case studies, practices report 4 to 7 percent more revenue after going live, against an ongoing 2 percent posting fee.

## Dentrix

Dentrix has anchored dental practice management for 30+ years and, according to the company, runs in 35,000+ US practices.

### What they offer

- All-in-one system tying scheduling, imaging, billing, analytics, and patient engagement
- Ascend automation for insurance eligibility and claims processing
- Real-time dashboards and smart reports for single or multi-location groups
- Built-in AI diagnostic tools for caries identification and treatment planning

Good for: Existing practices with Patterson Dental relationships wanting a mature, feature-rich system.

Limitation: Local installs need remote access, updates, and IT support that cloud-native options skip.

## Eaglesoft

According to Patterson Dental, Eaglesoft is used in nearly 30,000 practices and integrates with 55+ authorized software solutions.

### What they offer

- Deep digital imaging integration covering video, intraoral, and digital X-rays in a single patient record
- Open ecosystem for connecting third-party tools to customize workflows
- Eaglesoft Service Club with unlimited US-based support, free upgrades, and Schick warranty coverage
- HIPAA-compliant forms and processes baked in

Good for: Practices already invested in Patterson hardware and imaging equipment that want a single vendor for supplies and software.

Limitation: The interface looks like an older Windows app, and the learning curve is steep for new staff.

## Open Dental

Open Dental is highly customizable dental practice management software priced for clinics of any size. Its open-source foundation gives practices full data ownership and customization depth that proprietary systems can't match.

### What they offer

- Pricing from $199/month/location for up to three providers, dropping to $149/month after twelve months
- True data ownership with anytime export and no vendor lock-in
- eServices including patient portal, payments, web forms, scheduling, secure email, and integrated texting
- Wide third-party integration network through an extensive bridge library

Good for: Cost-conscious practices wanting data ownership without enterprise pricing.

Limitation: Primarily on-premise. Cloud hosting lags behind cloud-native options like Curve.

## Curve Dental

Curve is a fast-growing cloud-based dental practice management system running as a true all-in-one with scheduling, charting, billing, imaging, and patient engagement under one roof.

### What they offer

- No servers or IT overhead, with mobile access via Curve Mobile, HIPAA-compliant AWS encryption, automated backups, and zero-downtime updates

- AI-ready data structure powering clinical diagnostics and business analytics

Good for: Growth-focused practices and multi-location groups wanting cloud-native architecture without on-premise infrastructure.

Limitation: Insurance estimates can be inaccurate, forcing staff to revert to manual verification.

## Denticon

Denticon is cloud-based dental practice management software built for multi-location groups. Owned by Planet DDS and, according to the company, used in over 10,000 North American practices, it's positioned as a leading cloud PMS for growth-stage organizations.

### What they offer

- Organization-wide visibility across practices, clinicians, and patients for centralized control
- Treatment planning, native imaging, ortho modules, and voice-activated perio charting
- Multi-location scheduling with patient self-scheduling and family block bookings
- HIPAA-compliant secure cloud data storage

Limitation: Single-location practices often find the feature set heavier than needed, with onboarding work required to unlock full value.

Founded by early Robinhood and Superhuman product managers, Lassie is working on autonomous systems that handle the busywork

Currently operating in 700+ small businesses across 49 states, providing business owners with over 250,000 hours of labor each year

Lassie, the company building autonomous systems to run small businesses, announced it has raised $35 million in Series A financing, bringing its total capital raised to $47 million. The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with support from Night Capital, Rahul Vohra, founder and former CEO of Superhuman; Zach Perret, co-founder and CEO of Plaid; Taavet Hinrikus, co-founder and former CEO of Wise; Gokul Rajaram; and Brian Balfour, co-founder and CEO of Reforge.

AI can do a lot today. It writes software, passes bar exams, and generates realistic videos from simple prompts. But it can do so much more. It can help millions of small business owners by handling their busywork. Up until now, software has not removed this painstaking administrative work and has merely rearranged it. For the first time, software can interpret messy context, move across the endless systems that small businesses have, and do that work for an owner.

Nowhere is this more apparent than in doctors’ offices, the largest type of small businesses behind retail and food and beverage. A typical practice loses 100+ hours a month to administrative work and spends roughly $200,000 a year on staff that owners can barely find, let alone keep.

Today, Lassie’s agent goes into a practice's insurance portals, pulls reimbursements, reconciles them against records, updates the system-of-record, and verifies the funds in the bank. Operating in more than 700 practices across 49 states, Lassie currently provides businesses owners with over 250,000 hours of labor each year.

"Small business owners should be freed up from doing busywork, so they can focus on what they are passionate about," said Steijn Pelle, CEO and co-founder of Lassie. "After watching 700 businesses rely on Lassie to do a big part of their administration, I am convinced that the future is bright. They now use the time we save them to grow the business and spend more time with customers. And we are just getting started!”

“I am thrilled to partner with Steijn, Frédéric, and the team as they build towards one of the most important shifts in software: from tools that help businesses operate to agents that do the work,” said Alex Rampell, co-founder of Affirm and General Partner at a16z. “We think businesses will soon run themselves and Lassie is the perfect example that this is not a pipe dream. They are already making this a reality, providing many businesses with tens of hours of labor each month, and allowing business owners to focus on what they love doing, not busywork.”

Most importantly, Lassie has given me time back to focus on my patients, grow my practice, and spend time with my family.”

To accelerate Lassie’s growth and adoption, the company announced Alex Rampell, co-founder of Affirm and general partner of Andreessen Horowitz, will be joining Lassie’s Board of Directors. # Lassie Raises $35M in Series A Funding

-

June 4, 2026

Lassie, a San Francisco, CA-based company building autonomous systems for small businesses, raised $35M in Series A funding.

The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Night Capital, Rahul Vohra, founder and former CEO of Superhuman; Zach Perret, co-founder and CEO of Plaid; Taavet Hinrikus, co-founder and former CEO of Wise; Gokul Rajaram; and Brian Balfour, co-founder and CEO of Reforge.

Alex Rampell, co-founder of Affirm and general partner of Andreessen Horowitz, will be joining Lassie’s Board of Directors. In addition, Dr. Ed Zuckerberg and Jason Warnick, former chief financial officer of Robinhood, will be joining the company as advisors.

The raise brought the total amount to $47M.

The company intends to use the funds to expand operations and its development efforts.

Led by CEO Steijn Pelle, Lassie is an AI company that develops autonomous systems designed to eliminate administrative back-office work for small businesses. Its AI agents automate complex, labor-intensive workflows end-to-end, including:

- System Integration: automatically updating the clinic’s internal patient and practice management systems.
- Insurance Claim Management: accessing insurance portals directly to retrieve reimbursement data and submit claims.
- Revenue Cycle Management: reconciling accounts, verifying bank funds, and matching payments without human intervention.

Operating in more than 700 practices across 49 states, Lassie provides businesses owners with over 250,000 hours of labor each year.

Lassie Raises $35 Million in Series A Round Led By a16z

# Lassie Raises $35 Million in Series A Round Led By a16z

 2 minute read | June.04.2026 

Lassie, the company building AI-powered autonomous systems to run small businesses, announced its $35 million Series A financing, bringing its total capital raised to $47 million.

The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with support from Night Capital, Rahul Vohra (founder and former CEO of Superhuman), Zach Perret (co-founder and CEO of Plaid), Taavet Hinrikus (co-founder and former CEO of Wise), Gokul Rajaram and Brian Balfour.

Orrick represents Lassie.

## THE COMPANY

Lassie helps small businesses run themselves. By pushing the boundaries of autonomous systems, it handles the busywork for business owners. First, doctor’s offices.

Lassie was founded by Steijn Pelle, an early product manager at Robinhood and Coinbase, and Frédéric Renken, the first product hire of Superhuman. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, SV Angel, Homebrew, Go Global Ventures, Night Capital, and more. The company currently serves 700+ small businesses, providing owners with over 250,000 hours of labor each year.

## THE IMPACT

"Small business owners should be freed up from doing busywork, so they can focus on what they are passionate about," said Steijn Pelle, CEO and co-founder of Lassie. "After watching 700 businesses rely on Lassie to do a big part of their administration, I am convinced that the future is bright. They now use the time we save them to grow the business and spend more time with customers. And we are just getting started!"

## THE TEAM

Orrick’s John Bautista and Jake Wyrick lead the team advising Lassie, with support from Alexandra Aquilina-Piscitello, Vinny Mei, Alexa Steranko, Andrew Philip Barlow, Daniel Yost, Taylor Ranfos, Maya Krpata, Yvonne Nyborg, Blake Ilstrup and Dolph Hellman.

### Jake Wyrick Of Counsel

> Steijn Pelle is the co-founder and CEO of Lassie, a San Francisco AI company building an autonomous back-office worker that runs the financial admin of independent businesses, starting with dental and medical practices. A Dutch transplant to Silicon Valley with roughly 15 years in startups, he cut his teeth on consumer growth at HealthTap, Coinbase and Robinhood before founding Lassie in 2021.
